title: ping_l2 udp test: injected frame rejected as replay (-114) — same (epoch,seq) delivered or committed twice after soft reinit
description: Last ping_l2 failure (6/7 after 17nw fix cf9afa78a1). Trace on heft: queue_stats reinit window shows 2x 'TX frame build failed: no signing key (-126)' (startup MLD/ND racing the enable->reprovision window), then in test_udp_payload the injected UDP frame is RX-rejected 'replay detected (-114)' TWICE (00:00.350 and 01.250) and the UDP observer times out (-11). Candidates: (1) epoch_advance_for_boot returns the SAME epoch across soft deinit/init cycles on native_sim (persistence stubbed) while tx_seq resets to 0 on key reload, so frames reuse (epoch,seq) already committed by full_ping's exchange under the same peer key — i.e. epoch MUST advance per reinit or the replay table must be reset whenever the epoch resets (check init_link_ctx_locked replay_table_init ordering vs epoch selection); (2) the loopback driver double-delivering one frame after the one-shot change (arm-time rx_work submit racing the TX-path submit) — verify each frame is dequeued exactly once; (3) the IPv6 stack retransmitting (NS retransmit timer) the same compressed payload. Note the successful (non-logged) delivery path: a silent first delivery would mean the frame WAS committed once and the observer timeout is a socket-binding issue instead — instrument before assuming.
